issue_plan.name: Smooth Python application proof runs
issue_plan.summary: These six issues address the receipt, scheduling, driver and contract setup problems from the ask3d proof experiment. They expose the first harness error, preserve list-valued state, skip work whose prerequisites failed under the qualification rules on main including D-0416, and let each Python check use its own driver at larger bounds. They also identify the exact contract stand-in to copy from the application's pinned Invariant revision and, after #793 merges, document a refusal-decision function that qualifies through calls recorded on accepted and refused attempts. The statue service's larger-run slowdown remains for a separate investigation with the real tools and a precise follow-up fix.

issues.title: Show the first Python harness error in gate receipts
issues.body:
The ask3d experiment failed because hold was called without a selected call on an owned worker. The harness then wrapped its own error as "application call raised an undeclared or invalid refusal", and a last-20-lines summary hid the original cause. Make the receipt's What failed section identify the first harness error, including "hold requires a selected call on an owned worker" in this case, with the affected target and invocation.

Follow the failure from internal/verify/python_application_observer.py through execution and conformance reporting to internal/receipt. Preserve the first collector failure through exception chaining, poisoning and cleanup; a harness error must not be relabeled as an application refusal. Carry the useful cause into JSON diagnostics and the short receipt summary, including for a larger run that actually executes, while retaining the full diagnostic context. Do not depend on the first cause fitting in the last 20 traceback lines. Render application text safely and keep host-path normalization.

Acceptance must exercise the real collector with the invalid hold, a chain longer than 20 lines, and a later cleanup or poisoned-lifecycle error. Check both JSON and Markdown for the original cause and invocation identity. Genuine undeclared application exceptions must still fail, and valid declared refusals must still be checked as refusals under D-0279. No failed or incomplete stream gains accepted observations. Keep the timeout diagnostic regressions from #645 passing.

Update the affected receipt documentation and keep SPEC.md and README accurate under D-0122 and D-0294. Follow AGENTS.md for decision records and merger follow-up when the factory cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Preserve list-valued Python state in component receipts
issues.body:
Python module observations retain the statue service's task status list, such as [] becoming ["queued"], but component conformance rows turn it into an empty string. internal/verify/python_application_report.go currently calls conformance.Encode directly and discards its error; bare arrays require the module boundary's sequence conversion before they can be encoded.

Use the same module-value semantics as the conformance recording path when constructing component observation From and To values. Keep the existing map-of-TLA-value-strings component schema: a module list is an ordered TLA+ sequence, including the empty sequence, and nested lists and records retain their full values. Preserve scalar types, exact integers and list order. Handle conversion errors explicitly with the invocation and field identified rather than emitting an empty value. Keep the raw execution observations intact and preserve the existing semantics of non-module observations and attempted-step arguments.

Acceptance must drive sampled and explored module observations through component attribution and JSON/Markdown receipts. Cover [] to ["queued"], repeated and reordered elements, nested list/record values, empty lists versus empty strings, and integers beyond JavaScript's exact range. Assert agreement with the recording sent to TLC, safe literal rendering, and stable fingerprints after JSON round trips; changing a list value or its order must change the evidence fingerprint. Invalid values must produce a diagnostic, never silently disappear. Conformance qualifications must remain unchanged.

This repairs the evidence-preservation behavior of D-0170, D-0175, D-0199 and D-0333. Update the relevant Python evidence documentation and keep SPEC.md and README accurate, with decision handling as AGENTS.md requires.

issues.title: Skip Python checks whose prerequisites have failed
issues.body:
The Python application gate currently reruns failed explorations one size larger and invokes Nagini before discovering that a proof cannot qualify. Change this scheduling in internal/verify/python_application_gate.go and python_application_gate_proofs.go so dependent work is skipped with a reason, while independent evidence can still be collected.

For each exhaustive invocation, require a successful, complete execution and passing conformance at the ratified bounds, including its exhaustive-state and attempted-step obligations, before scheduling its larger run. If none is eligible, do not launch the larger TLC check. Record each omitted rerun as skipped because of its named prerequisite; it must not become a second required failure. Eligible invocations still run, and an actual larger-bound disagreement still fails the gate.

Before acquiring or launching Nagini for a selected target, evaluate only the already knowable prerequisites under the qualification rules on main when this issue is built, including D-0416 (#793): qualifying evidence that the application runs that same staged declaration, tested support for every trusted contract the input assumes, and an input with nothing disqualifying left unaccounted for. D-0416 lets a check name a function exploration must see called inside its entries; the collector records its arguments and result against its staged declaration. Calls on both accepted and refused attempts, in the same session, against the same source bytes and beside that check's passing conformance, qualify as same-function evidence even when exploration selects a different function. A named function that is never called or is called only on accepted attempts does not qualify through this route. Preserve every other qualification route, including conformance on the selected or held function, and consume #793's evidence rather than reimplementing its collection in this issue.

Skip Nagini only when these prerequisites rule out every applicable qualification route; never suppress a target that can qualify through D-0416's recorded calls. Do not treat the absence of a verifier result before Nagini runs as a failed prerequisite. A target with another qualifying conformance run remains eligible; an unrelated failed check or unused contract must not suppress its proof. Keep proof-input and stand-in preflight validation. Record an unrun proof explicitly, with its input identity and blocking reasons, without claiming a verifier run or success.

Acceptance must assert tool invocation counts as well as JSON and Markdown: failed base exploration is never rerun, blocked proof never starts Nagini, eligible sibling checks still execute, and all-success behavior is preserved. Cover mixed and all-skipped larger runs, failed assumed-contract support, alternate passing conformance, and existing missing-contract refusals. Include a refusal-decision function that is not the exploration's selected target but has qualifying calls recorded on accepted and refused attempts: Nagini must run for it, including when an unrelated check fails. Cover missing calls, accepted-only calls, mismatched source bytes and failed supporting conformance; block that recorded-call route without blocking another valid route. Skips preserve the original gate failure, grant no assurance and survive receipt requalification and fingerprint round trips.

Update docs/python.md and SPEC.md for this refinement of D-0199 and D-0260, including D-0416's qualification route; keep README accurate. Follow AGENTS.md's decision and merger requirements.

issues.title: Run each Python check's own driver at larger bounds
issues.body:
An existing Python application with multiple component checks must be able to put each check's conformance driver in its own file. Today python_application_session.go requires every invocation's script to equal the manifest's top-level conformance driver, and RunLarger in python_application_execution.go copies only that top-level file. This forced ask3d to multiplex targets through command-line arguments.

Resolve an explicit conformance invocation's driver from its selected check source and its script argument relative to working_dir. Require those to identify the same staged regular file, retaining the existing application-root, traversal and symlink checks. Use that driver for ordinary execution and startup import paths, then test its own bound declarations and rewrite only its private copy for RunLarger. Preserve the top-level manifest driver for legacy applications and compatibility with existing single-driver configurations; no new manifest field is needed.

Apply the preceding issue's prerequisite checks per invocation. A driver without all required bound constants does not disable larger checking of another eligible driver. Keep the shared model's larger TLC result reusable, but bind every actual larger run to its own original driver path/hash, rewritten path/hash, selected declaration and read-only overlay. Preserve the staged application, dependency image, arguments, environment, collector authentication and weakest-result aggregation.

Acceptance must include two targets with distinct driver files, one outside the top-level driver's directory, with different working directories and extra arguments. Show each runs at the ratified bounds and receives its own larger constants and provenance. Cover a driver without bounds, one failed base invocation, an actual larger mismatch, stale or wrong source hashes, escaped/symlink paths, cancellation and unchanged original bytes. Retain legacy and shared-driver coverage, including receipt and fingerprint round trips.

Update docs/python.md and SPEC.md to describe per-check drivers under the existing D-0181, D-0185 and D-0199 isolation and evidence rules. Keep README accurate and follow AGENTS.md for decision records.

issues.title: Identify the exact contract stand-in an application must ship
issues.body:
An in-place Python proof requires the application to ship Invariant's nagini_contracts runtime stand-in at its root, byte for byte. The gate already checks this in shipsNaginiStandIn, but its remedy only names internal/verify/naginiruntime. Make that check tell the user exactly which package to copy, tied to the Invariant revision their CI builds. This implements #794's permitted gate-check remedy; verification continues to check the application as shipped.

On a missing or mismatched package, identify the application destination, the expected __init__.py and contracts.py hashes, and the source package at the running Invariant build's exact revision when available. Explain that local verification must use the same revision pinned by the application's CI and give copy instructions from that revision, not from a moving branch. If build revision metadata is absent or the build is modified, say so explicitly, retain the exact expected-byte hashes, and direct the user to build/run the CI-pinned revision before copying; never invent a revision or claim it matches CI. The remedy must work from a packaged binary without assuming an Invariant source checkout is beside the application.

Retain D-0260's exact two-file package requirement, rejection of changed bytes, extra files and alternate nagini_contracts locations, and production-binding protections. A stand-in installed from PyPI or injected only into the gate's staging area does not satisfy the shipping requirement. Keep the check before application execution and Nagini.

Acceptance must cover a correct package, absent package/file, changed bytes, an extra file and a second package, plus known, unknown and modified build identity. Verify actionable diagnostics and copying from a pinned checkout into a fixture, without network access or automatic overwrites of application files. Check that the fixture imports the shipped package and that no tests, driver or Nagini starts after rejection.

Update docs/python.md with the revision-specific copy and upgrade procedure and keep SPEC.md and README accurate. Follow AGENTS.md for decision records.

issues.title: Document plain-value decision functions for Python proof
issues.body:
Build this issue only after #793 merges, using its recorded-call qualification under D-0416. Expand docs/python.md with the working pattern the ask3d experiment needed: a small pure decision function taking plain values, called by an ordinary application handler. The function decides whether a request is accepted or refused, as ask3d's admission() decides refusals such as 403, 400 and 409. Readers should be able to follow the example without reconstructing the experiment or interpreting the existing restriction tables.

Show the handler reading request/container/object state, deriving has_site: bool and site: str from an optional header, and passing those and any other needed scalar values into an undecorated synchronous decision function with supported inline Nagini contracts. Keep handler effects and container updates outside that function. Show the handler applying the function's decision: on refusal it exits through a declared refusal before the operation exploration selects is called; on acceptance it proceeds to that operation. Explain that pure describes its behavior here; the in-place gate does not admit the @Pure decorator. State the function's guarantee and distinguish it from tests of the handler and from checking callers' preconditions, which the gate does not prove.

Give small rejected/working pairs for all three reported limits: Optional/Union contract values may be read only in is, is not or isinstance tests; contracts cannot read subscripts, attributes or methods; and pinned Nagini 1.3.1 does not model dict.setdefault. Explain eager Python evaluation of Implies arguments and why an apparent guard does not make an Optional arithmetic/string operation safe. Move lookups and setdefault into the ordinary handler and pass their plain results into the decision function. Distinguish gate admission restrictions from Nagini's unsupported operation rather than suggesting the verifier or policy has changed.

Include the minimal component proof/conformance selection and exploration driver for the example, using the configuration #793 ships. Show the check explicitly naming the decision function whose calls exploration must record inside its entries, alongside the selection of that function for in-place proof. Explain that this refusal-decision function qualifies through those recorded calls under D-0416, not through conformance on the same selected declaration alone: a refused attempt exits before exploration's selected operation runs. The collector must record the decision function's arguments and result on both accepted and refused attempts in the same session, against the same staged source bytes, beside the check's passing conformance. Naming it without calling it, or calling it only on accepted attempts, does not qualify through this route. Link the exact stand-in setup instructions delivered by the preceding issue.

Verify the positive example against current admission, runtime execution with the shipped stand-in, passing exploration conformance, D-0416's recorded-call qualification and the pinned Nagini using the existing Python proof acceptance infrastructure. Cover accepted and refused attempts and absent and present headers, including an empty header; assert that the receipt qualifies the decision function through the recorded calls. Confirm that missing or accepted-only calls leave this example unqualified, and that the rejected contract examples fail for the stated reasons. This example adds no new claim that the handler, dependencies or whole application are proved.

Keep the explanation consistent with D-0260 as refined by D-0416 and the current SPEC.md. Update README only if its front-page guidance changes, respecting its 400-line limit and AGENTS.md's documentation and decision rules.
